newsitem.title: UK: Lead prices hit 10-month lows after LME inventory rise.
newsitem.headline: Lead prices hit 10-month lows after LME inventory rise.

text.p: Three months delivery lead moved to a 10-month low of $688 a tonne in early trading on Friday following another London Metal Exchange (LME) inventory rise.
Stocks rose by 5,475 tonnes to 121,850 -- the first time they have been over the 120,000-tonne since January.
Traders said trade liquidation moved the market lower against a backdrop of deteriorating charts and a lack of pick-up in demand for batteries.
Normally the winter months in the Northern hemisphere sparks buying for replacement automobile batteries, traders said.
Lead may fall further under long liquidation, though traders and analysts believe support is likely to kick in at $674.
A break below this level could see a slide towards $600.
On Thurday lead closed the LME kerb at $692 a tonne.
